Headline artefact is CRITICBENCH, a 15-dataset benchmark instrument for measuring critique-correct behaviour across 17 LLMs, not a loop mechanism; all measurement is lab-side.
Asks whether self-reflection helps at all once external feedback is disallowed, i.e. the value of the revision step; lab runs on TruthfulQA and HotpotQA with no real deployment.
Delta-view feedback plus fault localisation drives repair of an incorrect LaTeX extraction, so the claim is the revision step; evaluated by exact-match accuracy against GPT-4V in the lab.
Query2CAD's claim is its self-refinement loop that rewrites CAD macros from BLIP2 feedback; a prototype measured on an authors' dataset, not used in real design practice.
Analyses whether self-repair pays off and finds the bottleneck is feedback quality, i.e. the correction step; a lab analysis of Code Llama, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on HumanEval and APPS.
Actor-critic where the ASP solver is an off-the-shelf checker but the claim is iterative refinement from test-failure feedback (runner-up verification_and_gating); FOLIO accuracy in the lab.
Diagnoses self-evaluated feedback quality as the reflection bottleneck and proposes a contrast-derived checklist to drive re-examination; lab experiments on reasoning and translation tasks.
AlphaLLM closes an outer self-improving loop that upgrades the LLM from its own MCTS trajectories without annotations (runner-up deliberative_search); lab results on math reasoning.

RCoT's contrast with prior work is fine-grained rather than coarse feedback used to revise solutions (runner-up verification_and_gating for its reversal-based detection); lab runs on seven arithmetic datasets.

The claim is the peer-review arrangement itself, including confidence-weighted review exchange versus solution sharing and agent diversity; lab experiments over ten reasoning datasets.
ToT branches over candidate thoughts with lookahead and backtracking and self-evaluates which to expand, i.e. the exploration shape; a new prompting technique measured only in lab tasks.

AlphaVerus bootstraps itself across rounds by accumulating verifier-confirmed translations to seed later generations (runner-up deliberative_search for Treefinement); lab results on HumanEval and MBPP.

GIF-MCTS is a tree-search strategy that generates, improves and fixes candidate world models under a search budget (runner-up loop_evaluation_and_diagnosis for the CWMB suite); offline lab benchmarks.
Studies whether models revise an unethical output when given natural-language feedback, and at which scale that works; a prompting experiment on stereotyping tasks with no real deployment.
Volcano generates natural-language feedback on its own answer and rewrites it, so the claim is the revision step; a released model scored on MMHal-Bench, POPE and GAVIE in the lab.
MAgICoRe's claim is the refinement schedule: which problems get refined, how errors are localised, and how many rounds are enough; lab evaluation over seven reasoning datasets.
